final.memo:
We have examined the business and concluded that it falls squarely into our 'too hard' pile. While the company owns property/casualty and life-insurance franchises that theoretically mirror parts of our own, the business is burdened by an opaque, super-senior credit-default-swap portfolio [D01]. This structure creates uncontrollable liquidity risks and collateral demands that are fundamentally unquantifiable [D01], [D05].

Unlike standard insurance operations where we can rely on predictable underwriting and float, here the primary economics are driven by volatile derivative losses and asset impairments [D01]. The reported six-month net loss of $13.16 billion highlights the extreme instability facing the firm [D01]. We see no durable competitive advantage that can survive such capital volatility [D01], [D05].

Management has committed to a review of the business, but we cannot base an investment on the hope of a successful restructuring of such dangerous liabilities [D01]. Book value, at $29.04 per share, is a stale and unreliable metric in the current liquidity crisis [D02]. Without the ability to gauge the firm's true exposure, any attempt to value the company is mere speculation [D02], [D05].

We prioritize the safety of our capital above all else and refuse to engage in situations where the downside is a permanent loss of equity [D01]. We prefer to hold cash or T-bills rather than speculate on the survival of a financial institution with unbounded collateral obligations [D01], [D05]. We will continue to wait for opportunities that fall clearly within our circle of competence.
